12.1 Kinetic Pressure, Equipartition & Mean Free Path

A. Introduction & Learning Objectives

  • Connect microscopic molecular collisions to macroscopic pressure, temperature, and specific heats.

D. Physical Interpretation

Temperature is directly proportional to average translational kinetic energy of gas molecules.

B. Theoretical Explanation

Level 1 · Foundation Physics

Gas pressure arises from elastic momentum transfer of molecules colliding with container walls: P = ⅓ (N m / V) v_rms².

Level 2 · JEE Main

Average translational KE per molecule is (3/2) k_B T, independent of molecular mass! By equipartition, each quadratic degree of freedom carries ½ k_B T, giving C_v = (f/2)R and γ = 1 + 2/f.

Level 3 · JEE Advanced

For mixtures of n₁, n₂ moles with C_v1, C_v2, effective C_v,mix = (n₁C_v1 + n₂C_v2)/(n₁+n₂). Mean free path λ = 1 / (√2 π d² n_v).

C. Definitions & Fundamental Principles

Law of Equipartition
In thermal equilibrium, each quadratic energy mode averages ½ k_B T per molecule.

G. Assumptions & Limitations

  • Assumes point-sized non-interacting molecules undergoing elastic wall collisions.

I. Schematic Reference

Maxwell-Boltzmann Speed Distribution Curve

Peak shifts right and flattens as temperature increases; v_mp < v_avg < v_rms.

E. Mathematical Formulation

Molecular Speeds

vrms=3RTM,vavg=8RTπM,vmp=2RTMv_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}, \quad v_{\text{avg}} = \sqrt{\frac{8RT}{\pi M}}, \quad v_{\text{mp}} = \sqrt{\frac{2RT}{M}}vrms​=M3RT​​,vavg​=πM8RT​​,vmp​=M2RT​​

v_rms > v_avg > v_mp.

H. SI Units & Dimensional Formulae

Physical Quantity SI Unit Dimensions
Boltzmann Constant (k_B) J/K [M L² T⁻² K⁻¹]

J. Real-Life Applications

  • Escape of light hydrogen/helium from Earth’s atmosphere because their v_rms reaches a significant fraction of v_e.

K. Important Exam Concepts

  • Monoatomic f = 3 (γ=5/3); Rigid Diatomic f = 5 (γ=7/5); Non-linear Triatomic f = 6 (γ=4/3).

L. Common Mistakes & Fixes

Trap: Treating rotational energy as included in temperature scaling of monoatomic vs diatomic translational KE.

Fix: Translational KE per mole is ALWAYS (3/2)RT regardless of atomicity.

M. Conceptual Questions

Which has higher rms speed at 300 K: Hydrogen or Oxygen?

Hydrogen (M = 2 g/mol) is 4 times faster than Oxygen (M = 32 g/mol) since v_rms ∝ 1/√M.

O–Q. Advanced Techniques, Summary & Revision

Advanced Strategy

  • When connecting two vessels via a tap, conserve total moles n₁ + n₂ and total internal energy U₁ + U₂.

Summary & Revision Notes

  • P = ⅓ρv_rms²; γ = 1 + 2/f; v_rms > v_avg > v_mp.
  • k_B = R / N_A = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J/K.

F. Mathematical Derivation Engine (1)

Kinetic Theory Formula for Ideal Gas Pressure — Impulse-momentum theorem for elastic molecular wall collisions.

Assumptions

  • N molecules of mass m in cube of side L undergoing elastic collisions.

Symbols

  • v_rms — Root-mean-square molecular speed (m/s)

Step 1: Average force from one molecule bouncing across length L.

Δpx=2mvx,Δt=2Lvx  ⟹  F1=mvx2L\Delta p_x = 2 m v_x, \quad \Delta t = \frac{2L}{v_x} \implies F_1 = \frac{m v_x^2}{L}Δpx​=2mvx​,Δt=vx​2L​⟹F1​=Lmvx2​​

Step 2: By isotropy, v_x² = v_y² = v_z² = v²/3.

P=1L2∑i=1Nmvix2L=NmVvx2‾=13ρvrms2P = \frac{1}{L^2} \sum_{i=1}^N \frac{m v_{ix}^2}{L} = \frac{N m}{V} \overline{v_x^2} = \frac{1}{3} \rho v_{\text{rms}}^2P=L21​i=1∑N​Lmvix2​​=VNm​vx2​​=31​ρvrms2​

Final Result & Physical Significance

P=13ρvrms2P = \frac{1}{3}\rho v_{\text{rms}}^2P=31​ρvrms2​

Bridges Newtonian particle collisions directly with ideal gas law PV = nRT.

Worked Example: Calculate v_rms of O₂ (M = 0.032 kg/mol) at 300 K.

v_rms = √(3 × 8.314 × 300 / 0.032) = √(233,831) ≈ 483.6 m/s.

Answer: 483.6 m/s

N. Solved Problem Library (1)

Problem 1 · JEE Main · Molar-weighted heat capacity of ideal gas mixture JEE MAIN

Equal moles of Helium (γ₁ = 5/3) and Oxygen (γ₂ = 7/5) are mixed. Find the adiabatic index γ_mix of the mixture.

Given: n₁ = n₂ = n · C_v1 = 1.5 R, C_v2 = 2.5 R | Required: Effective γ_mix

Cv,mix=n1Cv1+n2Cv2n1+n2C_{v,\text{mix}} = \frac{n_1 C_{v1} + n_2 C_{v2}}{n_1 + n_2}Cv,mix​=n1​+n2​n1​Cv1​+n2​Cv2​​
γmix=1+RCv,mix\gamma_{\text{mix}} = 1 + \frac{R}{C_{v,\text{mix}}}γmix​=1+Cv,mix​R​
  1. C_v,mix = (1.5 R + 2.5 R)/2 = 2R.
  2. γ_mix = 1 + R / (2R) = 1.5 = 3/2.

Final Answer: 1.5 (3/2) · Strategy: Never average γ values directly—always average C_v first!

13.1 SHM Differential Equation, Springs & Pendulums

A. Introduction & Learning Objectives

  • Solve restoring-force oscillators, compute equivalent spring stiffness, and apply effective gravity to pendulums.

D. Physical Interpretation

Total energy E = ½kA² oscillates smoothly between potential energy (peaks at extremes) and kinetic energy (peaks at mean position).

B. Theoretical Explanation

Level 1 · Foundation Physics

SHM occurs whenever restoring force is directly proportional to negative displacement: F = −kx ⇒ a = −ω²x, with ω = √(k/m).

Level 2 · JEE Main

Springs in series share tension (1/k_eq = 1/k₁ + 1/k₂); springs in parallel share displacement (k_eq = k₁ + k₂).

Level 3 · JEE Advanced

Cutting a uniform spring of length L and stiffness k into fraction pL increases stiffness inversely: k_part = k / p. For a rigid physical pendulum, T = 2π √(I / (mgd)).

C. Definitions & Fundamental Principles

Angular Frequency (ω)
ω = 2π/T = √(k/m) governing SHM oscillation rate.

G. Assumptions & Limitations

  • Simple pendulum T = 2π√(L/g) assumes small angle sin θ ≈ θ (θ₀ < 10°).

I. Schematic Reference

SHM Phasor Circle & Sinusoidal Projection

Uniform circular motion projection gives x = A cos(ωt + φ).

E. Mathematical Formulation

SHM Solutions

x(t)=Asin⁡(ωt+ϕ),v=ωA2−x2,T=2πmkx(t) = A\sin(\omega t + \phi), \quad v = \omega\sqrt{A^2 - x^2}, \quad T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{m}{k}}x(t)=Asin(ωt+ϕ),v=ωA2−x2​,T=2πkm​​

Time period is amplitude-independent (isochronous).

H. SI Units & Dimensional Formulae

Physical Quantity SI Unit Dimensions
Spring Constant (k) N/m [M T⁻²]

J. Real-Life Applications

  • Quartz crystal oscillators in watches and tuned mass dampers in skyscrapers.

K. Important Exam Concepts

  • Effective gravity in accelerating lift or liquid buoyancy: T = 2π √(L / g_eff).

L. Common Mistakes & Fixes

Trap: Changing time period of a vertical spring-mass when moving to the Moon.

Fix: T = 2π√(m/k) depends only on mass and spring stiffness, NOT on gravity g!

M. Conceptual Questions

What is the frequency of kinetic energy oscillation compared to displacement frequency f?

2f, because K = ½mv² = ½mω²A² cos²(ωt) oscillates at double angular frequency 2ω.

O–Q. Advanced Techniques, Summary & Revision

Advanced Strategy

  • Use the circular phasor diagram to find exact time intervals between x = A/2 and x = A without algebraic ambiguity.

Summary & Revision Notes

  • a = −ω²x; T_spring = 2π√(m/k); T_pend = 2π√(L/g_eff).
  • k_spring ∝ 1/length; Series 1/k_eq = ∑ 1/k_i; Parallel k_eq = ∑ k_i.

F. Mathematical Derivation Engine (1)

Time Period of a Simple Pendulum for Small Oscillations — Tangential restoring torque balances rotational inertia about the pivot.

Assumptions

  • Point bob mass m, massless inextensible string L, small amplitude sin θ ≈ θ.

Symbols

  • θ — Angular displacement from vertical (rad)

Step 1: Apply small-angle approximation sin θ ≈ θ.

τ=−mgLsin⁡θ≈−mgLθ\tau = -mgL\sin\theta \approx -mgL\thetaτ=−mgLsinθ≈−mgLθ

Step 2: Set I = mL² and identify angular SHM frequency ω² = g/L.

Id2θdt2=(mL2)d2θdt2=−mgLθ  ⟹  d2θdt2=−gLθI\frac{d^2\theta}{dt^2} = (mL^2)\frac{d^2\theta}{dt^2} = -mgL\theta \implies \frac{d^2\theta}{dt^2} = -\frac{g}{L}\thetaIdt2d2θ​=(mL2)dt2d2θ​=−mgLθ⟹dt2d2θ​=−Lg​θ

Final Result & Physical Significance

T=2πω=2πLgT = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}T=ω2π​=2πgL​​

Pendulum period depends on local gravity g, enabling precision gravimetry.

Worked Example: Spring-mass m = 0.4 kg, k = 160 N/m. Find ω and T.

ω = √(160/0.4) = √400 = 20 rad/s. T = 2π/20 = π/10 ≈ 0.314 s.

Answer: ω = 20 rad/s, T = 0.314 s

Two identical springs of stiffness k each are connected in parallel to a mass m. What is the ratio of time period if they are reconnected in series to the same mass?

Given: k_parallel = 2k · k_series = k/2 | Required: Ratio T_series / T_parallel

T∝1keqT \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{k_{\text{eq}}}}T∝keq​​1​

Final Answer: 2 : 1 · Strategy: Stiffer parallel arrangement oscillates twice as fast (half the period).

14.1 Progressive Waves, Standing Waves, Organ Pipes & Doppler Effect

A. Introduction & Learning Objectives

  • Distinguish particle velocity from wave velocity, solve organ-pipe harmonics, beats, and relativistic-free acoustic Doppler shifts.

D. Physical Interpretation

Standing waves trap energy locally between fixed nodes without net energy transport along the medium.

B. Theoretical Explanation

Level 1 · Foundation Physics

A harmonic wave y(x, t) = A sin(kx − ωt) propagates along +x with wave speed v = ω/k = fλ. Transverse speed on a stretched string is v = √(T/μ).

Level 2 · JEE Main

Open organ pipes support all harmonics f_n = n v / (2L) (n = 1, 2, 3...), whereas closed organ pipes support only odd harmonics f_n = (2n − 1) v / (4L). Beat frequency equals |f₁ − f₂|.

Level 3 · JEE Advanced

The Doppler shifted frequency is f′ = f (v ± v_o) / (v ∓ v_s): signs in numerator and denominator follow directly from whether observer/source motion compresses or stretches wavefront spacing.

C. Definitions & Fundamental Principles

End Correction (e)
Antinode forms slightly outside open pipe end by e ≈ 0.6 r, replacing L with L + e (closed) or L + 2e (open).

G. Assumptions & Limitations

  • Acoustic Doppler assumes source and observer speeds are strictly subsonic (v_s, v_o < v).

I. Schematic Reference

Standing Wave Harmonics & Node-Antinode Envelope

Superposition of counter-propagating waves forms stationary nodes separated by λ/2.

E. Mathematical Formulation

String Wave & Doppler

v=Tμ,f′=f(v±vov∓vs)v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}}, \quad f' = f\left(\frac{v \pm v_o}{v \mp v_s}\right)v=μT​​,f′=f(v∓vs​v±vo​​)

Top signs for approach, bottom signs for separation.

H. SI Units & Dimensional Formulae

Physical Quantity SI Unit Dimensions
Wave Number (k = 2π/λ) rad/m [L⁻¹]
Linear Mass Density (μ) kg/m [M L⁻¹]

J. Real-Life Applications

  • Musical wind instruments, ultrasonic medical Doppler blood-flow imaging, and acoustic resonance tubes.

K. Important Exam Concepts

  • Loading a tuning fork with wax lowers its frequency; filing its prongs raises its frequency.

L. Common Mistakes & Fixes

Trap: Confusing maximum particle velocity ωA with wave propagation speed ω/k.

Fix: Wave speed v = ω/k depends on medium properties (T, μ); particle max speed v_p,max = ωA depends on amplitude!

M. Conceptual Questions

Why did Newton’s original isothermal formula underestimate the speed of sound in air by ~15%?

Rapid sound compressions are adiabatic, not isothermal; Laplace replaced P with γP = 1.4 P.

O–Q. Advanced Techniques, Summary & Revision

Advanced Strategy

  • When sound reflects off a moving wall, treat the wall first as a moving observer, then as a moving source re-emitting that shifted frequency.

Summary & Revision Notes

  • v = ω/k = √(T/μ); Closed pipe odd harmonics only; f_beat = |f₁ − f₂|.
  • Particle velocity v_p = −v (∂y/∂x); Node spacing = λ/2; Node-to-antinode = λ/4.

F. Mathematical Derivation Engine (1)

Standing Wave Equation & Node Locations — Linear superposition of two identical counter-propagating harmonic waves.

Assumptions

  • Equal amplitude A, frequency ω, and wavenumber k in a linear non-dispersive medium.

Symbols

  • k — Angular wavenumber 2π/λ (rad/m)

Step 1: Write forward and reflected wave displacements.

y1=Asin⁡(kx−ωt),y2=Asin⁡(kx+ωt)y_1 = A\sin(kx - \omega t), \quad y_2 = A\sin(kx + \omega t)y1​=Asin(kx−ωt),y2​=Asin(kx+ωt)

Step 2: Apply trigonometric sum-to-product identity sin(α−β)+sin(α+β) = 2 sin α cos β.

y=y1+y2=2Asin⁡(kx)cos⁡(ωt)y = y_1 + y_2 = 2A\sin(kx)\cos(\omega t)y=y1​+y2​=2Asin(kx)cos(ωt)

Step 3: Nodes occur where spatial amplitude envelope vanishes.

sin⁡(kx)=0  ⟹  kx=nπ  ⟹  x=nλ2\sin(kx) = 0 \implies kx = n\pi \implies x = \frac{n\lambda}{2}sin(kx)=0⟹kx=nπ⟹x=2nλ​

Final Result & Physical Significance

y(x,t)=2Asin⁡(kx)cos⁡(ωt),xnode=nλ2y(x, t) = 2A\sin(kx)\cos(\omega t), \quad x_{\text{node}} = \frac{n\lambda}{2}y(x,t)=2Asin(kx)cos(ωt),xnode​=2nλ​

Separates space and time completely, showing every point oscillates in phase within a loop.

Worked Example: String of mass 0.02 kg and length 2 m under tension 100 N. Find transverse wave speed.

μ = 0.02/2 = 0.01 kg/m. v = √(100 / 0.01) = √10000 = 100 m/s.

Answer: 100 m/s

N. Solved Problem Library (1)

Problem 1 · JEE Main · Beat frequency & filing effect JEE MAIN

A tuning fork A of unknown frequency produces 4 beats/s with a fork B of frequency 256 Hz. When A is slightly filed, the beat frequency rises to 6 beats/s. Find the original frequency of A.

Given: f_B = 256 Hz · Initial beats = 4 Hz · After filing A, beats = 6 Hz | Required: Original frequency f_A

fbeat=∣fA−fB∣f_{\text{beat}} = |f_A - f_B|fbeat​=∣fA​−fB​∣
  1. Initially f_A = 256 ± 4 ⇒ either 260 Hz or 252 Hz.
  2. Filing reduces inertia and INCREASES frequency f_A.
  3. If f_A was 252 Hz, increasing it brings it closer to 256 Hz, decreasing beats (contradicts 6 Hz). If f_A was 260 Hz, increasing it moves further away, increasing beats to 6 Hz.

Final Answer: 260 Hz · Strategy: Filing raises frequency; waxing lowers frequency—test both candidate roots.

In a particular system of units, force (FFF), acceleration (AAA), and time (TTT) are chosen as the fundamental physical quantities. Find the dimensions of energy in this system.

  4. It increases only if Poisson ratio is zero
View Answer & Solution (Ans: B)

Thermal expansion acts like a uniform photographic enlargement: every linear dimension between any two points on the solid—including across a cavity—expands by Δd=dαΔT\Delta d = d\alpha\Delta TΔd=dαΔT.
